issue.title: Log File Download and Ardupilot
issue.body:
Gents:
 Would I be correct to assume that the examples/logfile_download.cpp code has been tested against and runs properly with PX4? I haven't tested that myself but I have run it against Ardupilot. The stock code fails for the Ardupilot simulator, but this could certainly be due to differences between how PX4 and Ardupilot implement this functionality. 
 I tracked down the Ardupilot issue(s) (actually all related to the same issue) within log_files_impl.cpp and I can now successfully use the log file download functionally with Ardupilot. If there is the same issue with PX4 log files I'd be more than will to share the minor code fixes with this project.

Cheers

comments.body:
I'm confused what you're trying to say.

Please, if you find something doesn't work as expected: write down what PX4 or ArduPilot version you're using, the MAVSDK version, and what the error is, and best yet a small reproducible example (if there isn't already one).

Certainly, I can provide details.
From the Ardupilot console there is a single log file:
> LAND> 
LAND> log list
LAND> Requesting log list
Log 1  numLogs 1 lastLog 1 size 2366659 Mon Jan 26 16:03:34 2026

Running the _logfile_download_ from the examples directory:

> ./logfile_download udpout://127.0.0.1:14540 test
[04:02:39|Info ] MAVSDK version: v3.14.0-9-g1c642ab9 (mavsdk_impl.cpp:33)
[04:02:40|Debug] Component Autopilot (component ID: 1) added. (system_impl.cpp:496)
[04:02:40|Debug] Discovered 1 component (system_impl.cpp:616)
[04:02:40|Warn ] No logs available (log_files_impl.cpp:162)
LogFiles::get_entries failed: No Logfiles

It shows there are no log files available to download. 
Note, this is from the MAVSDK main branch.

FYI, here is the corresponding MavLink packet as decoded by Wireshark:

> No.     Time           Source                Destination           Protocol Leng
th Info
   2729 1.710707407    127.0.0.1             127.0.0.1             MAVLink 2.0 6
7     LOG_ENTRY
Frame 2729: 67 bytes on wire (536 bits), 67 bytes captured (536 bits) on interfa
ce lo, id 0
Ethernet II, Src: 00:00:00_00:00:00 (00:00:00:00:00:00), Dst: 00:00:00_00:00:00 
(00:00:00:00:00:00)
Internet Protocol Version 4, Src: 127.0.0.1, Dst: 127.0.0.1
User Datagram Protocol, Src Port: 14540, Dst Port: 47441
MAVLink Protocol (25)
    Header
        Magic value / version: 0xfd
        Payload length: 13
        Incompatible flags: 0x00
        Compatible flags: 0x00
        Packet sequence: 16
        System id: 0x01
        Component id: 0x01
        Message id: 0x00000076
    Payload: LOG_ENTRY (118)
        time_utc (uint32): 1769474756
        size (uint32): 2369564
        id (uint16): 1
        num_logs (uint16): 1
        last_log_num (uint16): 1
    Message CRC: 0x3ce5

> I tracked down the Ardupilot issue(s) (actually all related to the same issue) within log_files_impl.cpp and I can now successfully use the log file download functionally with Ardupilot. If there is the same issue with PX4 log files I'd be more than will to share the minor code fixes with this project.

May I ask what the minor code fixes were? Shouldn't they be applied to MAVSDK? Even if they only apply to Ardupilot, MAVSDK is trying to support Ardupilot so it's worth it! 😊

Given I haven't run PX4, I haven't seen its LOG_ENTRY packet in response to the LOG_REQUEST_LIST packet but I suspect the issue relates to the LOG_ENTRY packet. Below is the packet when 3 logs are present:

> No.     Time           Source                Destination           Protocol Length Info
   1070 2.193193647    127.0.0.1             127.0.0.1             MAVLink 2.0 67     LOG_ENTRY
Frame 1070: 67 bytes on wire (536 bits), 67 bytes captured (536 bits) on interface lo, id 0
Ethernet II, Src: 00:00:00_00:00:00 (00:00:00:00:00:00), Dst: 00:00:00_00:00:00 (00:00:00:00:00:00)
Internet Protocol Version 4, Src: 127.0.0.1, Dst: 127.0.0.1
User Datagram Protocol, Src Port: 57241, Dst Port: 14550
MAVLink Protocol (25)
    Header
        Magic value / version: 0xfd
        Payload length: 13
        Incompatible flags: 0x00
        Compatible flags: 0x00
        Packet sequence: 64
        System id: 0x01
        Component id: 0x01
        Message id: 0x00000076
    Payload: LOG_ENTRY (118)
        time_utc (uint32): 1769525010
        size (uint32): 12004244
        id (uint16): 1
        num_logs (uint16): 3
        last_log_num (uint16): 3
    Message CRC: 0x613b

Note that the **id** is 1 and the **num_logs** is 3.
The following code snippet from log_files_impl.cpp is of interest:
```
  // Store entry at direct index
    _log_entries[msg.id] = new_entry;

    // Check if all entries are received
    bool all_received =
        std::all_of(_log_entries.begin(), _log_entries.end(), [](const auto& entry_opt) {
            return entry_opt.has_value();
        });

```
The **new_entry** is stored at **_log_entries[msg_id]**, which in this case is **1**. The following code then returns **all_received** as **false** since **_log_entries[0]** is empty.
My suspicion is the PX4 LOG_ENTRY packet starts with an id=0. 
I'm not an Ardupilot developer so I have no idea with regards to the implications of changing the LOG_ENTRY packet data.

Hope this helps some.

issue.title: log_files: support ArduPilot, fixup example

repository.name: MAVSDK
repository.description: API and library for MAVLink compatible systems written in C++ 20

issue.body:
This supports log files for ArduPilot where they are 1 based, not 0 based like PX4 does it.

The PR also fixes up a double promise, the example arg parsing, as well as the example file extensions.

Thanks to @flybratten04 for pointing this out.

Closes https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/issues/2753.
